title: Taxi associations’ Luanda stoppage and street blockades
location: Luanda, with Benfica described as an epicenter and blockades on major streets; BANTUMEN also reports strike activity in nine other provinces without site-specific gathering evidence.
organizer: ANATA, ATA and ATL taxi associations
participants_original: No demonstrator count is reported. CIAM/Jornal de Angola reports more than 40,000 taxi drivers across vehicles, fleets and individual operators, not participants at a gathering; the thousands walking were commuters.
threshold_50_evidence: S002 reports pickets and barricades; S007 reports drivers blocking major Luanda streets. Neither counts people in a public gathering. S005’s over-40,000 figure is a taxi/driver stoppage figure, not protest attendance. The 50-person threshold is unresolved.

occurrence.summary: Novo Jornal reports pickets/barricades and BANTUMEN reports drivers blocking major streets during the 10 January stoppage.

start_date.summary: Both bodies date the taxi stoppage and associated street activity to 10 January 2022.

end_date.summary: RNA says the associations suspended the stoppage and taxis returned to service on 12 January; this is the last reported stoppage day, not proof of the physical end of any separate gathering.

location.summary: Luanda is the documented site; BANTUMEN identifies Benfica as an epicenter and reports blocked major streets. Reports of nine additional provinces concern strike extent and do not establish qualifying gatherings there.

organizer.summary: ANATA, ATA and ATL are named as the taxi associations behind the stoppage.

demands.summary: Associations cite police treatment/excessive zeal, exclusion from government policy, and COVID passenger-capacity restrictions. Category assignment is provisional; the reported demands also include professionalization and road/route concerns.

participants_original.summary: None of these bodies counts demonstrators; S002’s pedestrians were commuters and S005’s 40,000 refers to taxi operators/vehicles/fleets.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Street blockades/pickets are established, but no public-gathering headcount is given; the unrelated operator/stoppage figure cannot be used as protest attendance.

protester_violence.summary: Vandalism is reported, but BANTUMEN records association denials and S005 says association presidents disavowed responsibility; attribution to the demonstrators remains unresolved.

state_response.summary: Arrests are reported: police quoted by BANTUMEN said 17 were detained, an association president told CIAM/Jornal de Angola that over 100 associated drivers/delegates had been detained, and the interior minister later reported 102 suspects detained. These are differing attributed counts/times, not attendance. Talks were planned, but no meeting, agreement or accommodation is established; other response dimensions are unknown.

state_target.summary: Reported grievances concern police treatment, government exclusion and state-imposed passenger-capacity/route rules, though the exact seven-item demand list and which items were pressed in the street action require follow-up.

notes: Keep this Luanda candidate local. The strike reportedly extended to nine other provinces, but no province-specific public-gathering size is established. CIAM reproduces Jornal de Angola and is not independent corroboration. The end date refers to resumption of taxi service on 12 January. Do not treat vehicle/driver totals, detainees, or commuters as attendees.
open_questions: Did any specific Luanda picket or blockade involve at least 50 people?
Which association grievances were explicit public demands to the state, and which concerned professional or route matters?
Can vandalism be attributed to participants despite association denials?
Did the planned talks occur or produce any accommodation?
Were qualifying public gatherings reported in any of the nine additional provinces?

title: Luanda gathering following the 23 January police shooting
location: Via Expressa between Benfica and Viana, Luanda; VOA also locates unrest near Mutamba. Novo Jornal mentions Pedonal da Mutamba, but its relation to the Via Expressa incident is unclear.
organizer: Not identified; reports describe groups of young people/citizens.
participants_original: Novo Jornal’s lead says groups of dozens; a later passage says hundreds of youths/citizens. VOA provides no crowd estimate.
threshold_50_evidence: Novo Jornal’s later body passage describes hundreds of youths/citizens, a qualitative count above 50; its lead instead says dozens. This single-source internal discrepancy is retained. VOA does not provide a number.

occurrence.summary: Novo Jornal calls the episode popular protests/tumult after a fatal police shooting; VOA describes unrest following the same event.

start_date.summary: Both bodies date the fatal shooting and ensuing gathering to Sunday, 23 January 2022.

end_date.summary: Novo Jornal says road activity lasted a little over an hour and police reinforcements reopened the road and controlled the tumult; the episode therefore ended on 23 January, with no exact end time.

location.summary: Novo Jornal identifies Via Expressa between Benfica and Viana; VOA says Via Expressa near Mutamba/Viana. Novo Jornal also mentions Pedonal da Mutamba without clarifying its relation to the blockade.

organizer.summary: Neither outlet identifies an organizer; both refer to groups of young people/citizens.

demands.summary: The gathering followed a fatal police shooting, supporting a provisional police-brutality issue code. Neither body reports slogans or a clearly articulated demand, so state-directed demand remains unresolved.

participants_original.summary: Novo Jornal says “groups of dozens” in its lead and later “hundreds”; VOA gives no count.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The later qualitative “hundreds” description exceeds 50, though the same article’s lead says dozens. No exact numeric estimate is published.

protester_violence.summary: Reports describe burning tires, public-property damage, attempted burning/damage to a bus, and an assault on the officer who fired; the officer was seriously injured.

state_response.summary: Novo Jornal reports police reinforcements reopening the road and controlling the tumult (crowd dispersal). Neither body reports arrest, beating, accommodation, protester killing, or shooting during the gathering. The fatal shot preceded the gathering and the victim’s protester status is not established; it is not coded as a response killing/shooting.

state_target.summary: Police conduct is the reported trigger and the event is described as protest/unrest after the shooting, but neither account supplies explicit slogans or a demand; eligibility awaits review of whether this is a qualifying demand directed to the state.

notes: The fatal shooting precedes the gathering. The victim may not have been a demonstrator; his membership is not established. Family and police accounts conflict about whether the shot was direct or a ricochet. Keep this event separate from the 10 January taxi unrest. Qualitative turnout supports the threshold provisionally, but the state-directed demand and exact location remain unresolved.
open_questions: Did attendees articulate a demand to the state, or was this solely immediate tumult after a death?
Does the later “hundreds” description refer to the same group as the lead’s “dozens”?
What is the relationship between the Via Expressa and Pedonal da Mutamba references?
Was the victim a member of the later crowd?
Can any contemporaneous independent/local source clarify attendance, trigger, or end time?
